nutrient-classes.def: The six kinds of substance food supplies: carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, vitamins, minerals and water. Macronutrients (carbohydrates, lipids, proteins and water) are needed in grams a day; micronutrients (vitamins and minerals) in milligrams or micrograms.

essential-nutrients.def: Nutrients the body cannot make, or cannot make fast enough, so they must come from food: the nine essential amino acids, the essential fatty acids linoleic and alpha-linolenic acid, and every vitamin and mineral.

vitamins.def: Organic molecules needed in small amounts that the body cannot make in enough amounts; most act as coenzymes or other active molecules and supply no energy. The fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) are stored and can build up; the water-soluble ones (the B vitamins and C) are stored little, except B12.

minerals.def: Inorganic elements needed from food. Major minerals, such as calcium, sodium and potassium, are needed at more than 100 mg a day; trace minerals, such as iron, zinc and iodine, at less.

calories.def: The energy food releases when broken down, measured in kilocalories: the heat that raises 1 kg of water by 1 °C. Carbohydrate and protein supply about 4 kcal per gram, fat about 9, and alcohol about 7.
